chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“If a man says, ‘You are a khunthā’ and ‘You are a pig,’ there is no hadd in that, but in it there is admonition and some punishment.”

key_terms.الْعُقُوبَةِ: punishment; here indicating a discretionary penalty
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a fixed legally prescribed punishment in Islamic law
key_terms.خُنْثَى: a person described as intersex; here used as an insulting attribution
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: pig; here used as an abusive insult

ai.seo_question: Does calling someone insulting names incur a hadd punishment in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that certain insulting expressions do not incur the fixed hadd punishment. However, they are still blameworthy and warrant admonition and a discretionary form of punishment.
